claim_blocked: The same PPO harness, task contract, and hyperparameters differ only by simulator.

finding.original_defect: VRX and Gazebo both sourced goal-relative position, velocity, and yaw from simulator odometry; acceleration and angular rate also fell back to odometry when IMU was absent.
finding.ground_velocity_source: Timestamped finite difference of consecutive noisy NavSat fixes; no Odometry twist enters the observation.
finding.goal_relative_position_source: Noisy, delayed NavSat position in local NED; no Odometry pose enters the observation.
finding.imu_source: sensor_msgs/Imu linear acceleration, angular velocity, and orientation quaternion, converted from FLU/ENU to body-NED/NED yaw. Missing or stale IMU zero-fills all seven IMU fields.
finding.classification: oracle fallbacks removed in shared VRX/Gazebo TaskTraceBridge
finding.noise_model: GPS is sampled at 2 Hz, held between fixes, delayed 0.2 s, and receives seeded independent 0.8 m horizontal position noise. NavSatFix has no ground velocity, so velocity is differenced from noisy position.

source_trace.evidence: The generated model enables gz::sim::systems::OdometryPublisher on the odometry topic; NavSat is a separate sensor.
Odometry remains privileged trace state only. NavSatFix is conditioned through ExternalGpsModel; Imu supplies acceleration, angular rate, and yaw.
The runtime now uses the same ExternalGpsModel and explicit Imu conversion; it does not serialize odometry as sensor observation data.
The trace conversion forwards separate explicit imu and gps samples alongside privileged state.

The 17-field observation accepts explicit fresh IMU/GPS samples only. Missing, invalid, future, or stale samples are zero-filled; no odometry fallback exists. This shared bridge also closes the Gazebo defect.

comparison_with_bcod_sim: Position rate, hold, latency, and horizontal noise now match bcod-sim defaults. Velocity cannot match: bcod-sim emits an independently modeled 0.08 m/s GPS velocity, while ROS NavSatFix has no velocity and differencing independent 0.8 m position errors at 2 Hz amplifies stationary velocity noise to about 2.26 m/s analytically.

residual_measurement.kind: deterministic synthetic stationary NavSat stream; not a live VRX/Gazebo measurement

verification.oracle_exclusion_regression: passed for both VRX and Gazebo adapters; changing every privileged odometry field leaves the 12 sensor observation fields unchanged
verification.missing_and_stale_policy: passed; missing, invalid, future, and stale samples zero-fill rather than falling back to odometry
verification.live_topic_trajectory_measurement: outstanding; the checked-in harness validates SDF/exporter launch only and has no connected episode lifecycle or Transport trace process

required_resolution_order: Run matched live VRX and Gazebo trajectories under pinned runtimes and verify the sensor topics, timestamps, 2 Hz hold, 0.2 s release delay, frames, and empirical errors.
Decide explicitly whether the approximately 27x GPS velocity-noise mismatch is accepted, filtered with documented additional latency, or resolved by a uniform contract revision.
Regenerate conformance traces only after that decision; do not train while Gate A is blocked.
decision.recommended_next_action: Perform live runtime validation for both VRX and Gazebo. Static and deterministic tests prove oracle exclusion, but cannot establish simulator topic behavior or empirical trajectory errors.
